nodes.name: When Called
nodes.notes: Called by every WhatsApp send/receive point. direction is in|out, actor is customer|ai|system|human_agent.

nodes.name: Already Logged?
nodes.notes: Idempotency: Meta retries a webhook delivery when n8n is slow to answer 200. alwaysOutputData=true so an empty result still emits one empty item, matching the processed_emails pattern in the Commitment Gate.

nodes.name: New Message?
nodes.notes: TRUE = no row found (empty item from the lookup) -> log it. FALSE = already logged -> stop.

nodes.name: Find Open Conversation
nodes.notes: Every conversation for this phone number. Resolve Session picks the newest. Do not add a sort + limit 1 here: the node's sort option is not applied, so limit 1 returns the OLDEST row and every message gets pinned to the first conversation ever opened for that number.

nodes.name: Need New Conversation?
nodes.notes: TRUE = open a new conversation. FALSE = the item already is the conversation row to reuse. The operator must be boolean/true: needs_new_conversation is a boolean, and a string 'notEmpty' test reads false as the non-empty text 'false', which sends every message down the create branch.

nodes.name: Insert Message
nodes.notes: Append-only. This table is the source of truth; the transcript on the conversation is derived from it.

nodes.name: Update Conversation
nodes.notes: Full rewrite of the transcript, never an append. A lost update is corrected by the next message.

meta.note: Conversation history logger. Messages is the source of truth; Conversations.transcript is a read model rebuilt from it on every turn. Table ids are placeholders until the production tables exist - see scripts/create-conversation-tables.mjs.
